clue.text: Fracas on set making extra work

parts.note: surface reading: a brawl breaking out on a film set
setter's reading: work for film extras, who fill the background as a throng

explanation.surface: A punch-up on a film set means everyone has to stay late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra work' reads as overtime, but extras are the hired background actors in a film, and a mass scene is what they are hired for.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene with a throng of people on screen is the kind of job film extras are booked for.

clue.text: Cost of heraldic device

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a price asked for something
second meaning: a figure borne on a coat of arms

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the price of a coat of arms, but each half is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the price demanded for a service and the heraldic term for an emblem placed on a shield.

clue.text: Spoken but not written in some minor alphabets

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: Some lesser-known scripts are only spoken, never set down in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means passed on by mouth, as opposed to written down.

clue.text: Remove hair of French-Roman governor

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
Pontius Pilate, Roman governor of Judaea

explanation.surface: Someone shaves a French-born Roman governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' supplies a French word, de; Pontius Pilate is the governor who tried Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: To depilate is to strip hair from the body, a formal word for removing hair.

clue.text: Girl having to change direction by a sidewise somersault

parts.note: a girl's name
to wheel is to turn round to face another way

explanation.surface: A girl must swerve because of a sideways tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer names a firework and also, in older usage, a cartwheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catherine wheel was an old name for a cartwheel, the gymnastic sideways roll on hands and feet.

clue.text: Egg king to change tea for fertiliser

indicators.note: to change these letters is to alter their order

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
R, from Rex, is king
the three letters of tea, rearranged

explanation.surface: A king trades his tea for plant food, of all things.
explanation.walkthrough: R for king comes from Latin rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates such as sodium nitrate are spread on fields to supply nitrogen, so a nitrate is a fertiliser.

clue.text: Quarrel with soldier taking composer outside

indicators.note: the composer's name is wrapped around the soldier, so it sits on the outside of him

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier

explanation.surface: A man falls out with a soldier who has dragged a composer outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are the usual crossword soldiers; here the composer's name is split after its first letter to hold them.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a rift or falling-out between people, so it can stand as a noun for a quarrel.

clue.text: Examine or discuss motive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to think or argue a matter through
second meaning: the grounds behind an action

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a verb, the second a noun; the word serves as both.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to argue logically about something; as a noun it is the cause or grounds for doing it.

clue.text: A WD car-engineer turned philanthropist…
Puma springing to gallery is cut off

indicators.note: a big cat springing leaps about, so the letters of its name jump into a new order

parts.note: the four letters of the cat, rearranged
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A puma leaping at a gallery visitor is a frightening scene, with something being cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London art gallery, a crossword staple for TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To amputate is to sever a limb surgically, so the verb means to cut off.

clue.text: Musicians with unusual role for streamer

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so these letters take an altered order

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
the four letters of role, rearranged

explanation.surface: Band members find an odd job for someone throwing streamers at a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A banderol is a long narrow flag or pennant flown from a mast or lance, a kind of streamer.

clue.text: General direction on ground to be made up

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
a way is a direction, as in 'which way?'

explanation.surface: A general's line of march across the battlefield remains undecided.
explanation.walkthrough: General Lee is a crossword stock figure. The definition reads off the phrase 'leeway to make up': lost ground still to be regained.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is lost time or progress that must be recovered, the idiom being that one has leeway to make up.

clue.text: Stick to the book and be consistent

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; 'be' goes with it as a phrase

parts.note: to cohere is to stick together
NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Follow the rules and don't change your story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick to the book' reads as one idiom, but 'to' only joins the verb to the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A coherent argument holds together logically, which is what being consistent means.

clue.text: … to make man re turn to the cloth
Got to dine out on refurbished boat

indicators.note: a refurbished vessel has been taken apart and refitted, so its letters are rearranged
dining out is a jaunt away from home, and here the word puts the letters out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets to have a dinner on board a newly refitted boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got to' looks like 'had the chance to', but the definition is 'Got' alone; two separate words are each rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtained is the past tense of obtain, to acquire, matching got in the sense of acquired.

clue.text: What shot may be appealing to umpire?

parts.note: surface reading: a remark on how good a cricket stroke or photograph was
setter's reading: the fielders' shouted appeal for a batsman to be given out

explanation.surface: A shot in cricket draws an appeal to the umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders shout this question at the umpire to ask for a batsman to be given out; a shot can also be a photo shown off with the same words.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket appeal is the fielding side's formal request that the umpire rule the batsman out.

clue.text: Rhetorical metaphor for sailor held by word of honour

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: parole is a prisoner's word of honour
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A speaker reaches for a figure of speech about a sailor who keeps his promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Parabole is the rhetorical term for a comparison or simile, a figure of speech akin to a metaphor.

clue.text: Primitive life-form awfully lax about tool production

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a mangled order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A simple creature is sloppy about making tools.
explanation.definitionFit: The axolotl is a Mexican salamander that keeps its larval form for life, an amphibian often called primitive.

clue.text: Oriental nonsense from ancient Jewish ascetic

indicators.note: the word itself says sense has been made senseless, so those letters come out jumbled

parts.note: E for East, the Orient
the second half of the word, sense, with its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: An Eastern guru talks drivel, says an old Jewish holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonsense' splits in two: sense made into nonsense is jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were a Jewish sect of the Second Temple period known for an austere, communal and ascetic life.

clue.text: Tree on estuary getting distemper

parts.note: the lime, or linden, is a tree
the Wash is a large estuary on England's east coast

explanation.surface: A tree by a river mouth catches a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Distemper reads as the dog disease, but it is also a cheap water-based paint. The Wash is a broad bay and estuary between Lincolnshire and Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Limewash is a whitewash for walls, of the same family of cheap water-based paints as distemper.

clue.text: Indian doctor gets the bird

parts.note: MO, Medical Officer, is a doctor
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: An Indian physician is rudely dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' reads as being booed off; here the bird is just a hawk. Indian means a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are a Native American people of the Iroquois confederacy, so one is an American Indian.

clue.text: Sent out to leading Devon town

indicators.note: letters sent out are scattered, so they arrive in another order
a word that is leading goes in front, so it starts the answer

parts.note: taken as written
the four letters of sent, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is dispatched to the chief town in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Totnes is a market town in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Totnes is a historic market town on the River Dart in Devon, so it is an example of a Devon town.

clue.text: Accomplished by vice-head, perhaps

parts.note: surface reading: a job finished by a deputy head teacher
setter's reading: a vice-head has been made 'a chief', so the word is heard as a-chief-ed

explanation.surface: A task got done by the deputy head of a school.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on sound: the answer, spoken, resembles 'a chief' plus -ed, which fits someone promoted to vice-head. The wordplay is a guess: there is no published key yet.
explanation.definitionFit: To have achieved something is to have brought it to a successful finish, a plain synonym of accomplished.

clue.text: Some chaps entering rear of church

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: A few men walk into the back of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' looks like a container signal, but it is part of the run the letters lie in.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the rounded recess at the east end of a church, behind the altar.

clue.text: Has a yearning for fruit on old vessel

parts.note: one who longs has a yearning
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: Someone craves fruit while aboard an ancient ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has a yearning for fruit' reads as one craving, but 'for' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A longship is the long oared warship used by the Vikings, so it is a vessel from long ago.

clue.text: Pianist as mason?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Fats ..., the American jazz pianist
second meaning: one who builds walls

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is a coinage: someone who builds walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas 'Fats' Waller was a famous stride pianist, and a builder of walls in stone would be one who walls.

clue.text: Rocket when athlete has to run without clothes

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University
to streak is to run naked in public

explanation.surface: An athlete is made to run naked, a pun on someone rocketing along.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsman; Blue Streak was a 1950s-60s British ballistic missile and launcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Streak was a British rocket developed as a missile and later used as a launcher's first stage.
